title: Paloma and the Orchard
premise: Ulyana Vane, a widowed single father running the last bookshop in the orchard town of Palomara, has spent five years training his heart into obedience. When his formidable family descends for the annual reunion, he hires Paloma Reyes—a traveling restorer hired to repair the shop's flood-damaged stock—to pose as his partner for one weekend. But the pretense curdles into something real, and Ulyana discovers the family estate, and the orchard itself, are being quietly sold out from under the town by his own brother. To save both the shop and the trees his late wife planted, Ulyana must forgive himself for surviving her, claim a love he never planned, and choose found family over blood duty—ending with him signing the deed to the orchard over to the town, hand in hand with Paloma beneath the blossoms.
about_author: R. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former orchard bookkeeper who spent two decades cataloguing love letters found in secondhand novels before writing any of their own. They live between two coasts and one very opinionated lemon tree.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A burst pipe floods Vane & Daughter Books, and Paloma arrives to restore the waterlogged stock—brisk, unimpressed, allergic to sentimentality. Their friction crackles. Emotional beat: grief disguised as routine; Ulyana insists everything broken can be dried flat and contained.

chapters.title: Reunion Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The invitation to the Vane family reunion arrives with a plus-one expectation and his mother's pointed phone call. His daughter, Wren, casually tells an aunt that Papa 'has someone.' Cornered, Ulyana makes Paloma an absurd offer: one weekend, paid in restored first editions. Beat: panic dressed up as practicality.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma negotiates the fake-date contract with dry humor and hidden curiosity, laying down rules: no pasts, no promises. Wren interviews her like a customs officer and approves. Beat: reluctant warmth; Paloma recognizes a fellow person who keeps feelings in ledgers.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The reunion begins at the family estate above the orchard. The performance works too well—his mother softens, rivals gawk—and Ulyana finds himself defending Paloma's honor without being asked. Beat: the dangerous pleasure of being believed.

chapters.title: By Dessert
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During dessert, a cousin needles Ulyana about his wife, and Paloma improvises a story so tender it silences the table—and herself. Later, on the orchard path, they almost kiss and don't. Beat: the contract cracking from the inside.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Hides
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Snooping for wine, Ulyana overhears his brother Marcus negotiating the sale of the orchard to a resort developer—the same land Wren plays in, the same trees his late wife planted. He says nothing, ashamed of how easily he was excluded. Beat: dread and self-blame entwined.

chapters.title: Rain on the Trellis
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Trapped by a storm in the shop's back room, Paloma and Ulyana finally trade real histories—her exiled family, his guilt over surviving the crash. They cross the line they drew in chapter three. Beat: intimacy as surrender, not conquest.

chapters.title: The Family Business
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Marcus confronts Ulyana, revealing he knew about the fake relationship and threatens to expose it at the reunion's final dinner unless Ulyana signs consent papers legitimizing the sale. Ulyana realizes his silence made him complicit. Beat: the low point—duty weaponized against love.

chapters.title: Everything True at Once
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the final dinner, Marcus springs the trap—but Ulyana stands first, confessing the fake date, the eavesdropping, and the sale, then asks the family to choose the orchard over the payout. Wren backs him; the town arrives with petitions. Beat: climax—truth as the only viable strategy.

chapters.title: Paloma and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, closing with Paloma's. The deal collapses; the family, shamed by matriarch Elena's defection, deeds the orchard to a town trust. In spring, the trees bloom, the shop reopens with restored books, and Ulyana asks Paloma to stay—not as a hire, but as home. Beat: forgiveness of the man in the mirror; love chosen freely.
